method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the fixed-point application and partial-selector diagonal, with exact formula, macro, label and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Defining functions from their indices and impossibility of a partial computable procedure that extracts characteristic-function indices from all computable c.e. sets.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The fixed-point theorem lets a program use its own index; in particular some e satisfies φ_e(y)=e+y for every y. The same proof mechanism can design a self-printing Java or C++ program.
samples.checks: The index e, universal y, exact addition formula and two programming-language names are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: W_e is the domain of φ_e and the W_0,W_1,... list enumerates all c.e. sets. Although some W_e are computable, no partial computable f can, for every such e, halt with an index f(e) whose program computes the characteristic function of W_e.
samples.checks: The indexed-domain meaning, c.e. class, partial candidate, required definedness and characteristic-function condition are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For an arbitrary partial computable f, apply the fixed-point theorem to partial g(x,y) that returns zero only when y=0 and the universal program indexed by f(x) halts on zero with output zero. The resulting e has W_e={0} if that output is zero and W_e=empty otherwise. If f(e) diverges, the selector's required definedness fails; if it returns an index, that program gives the wrong membership answer at zero. The frozen proof had started with only a total computable f, which was insufficient for the theorem.
samples.checks: Both displayed case functions, the universal simulation order, zero-input diagonal, two possible W_e sets and partial-f divergence case are retained. OLCMP-024 documents the prose-only scope repair.

source_observations: OLCMP-024 corrects the proof quantifier from total to partial computable f and explicitly handles divergence of f(e) in the final prose; all protected formulas remain unchanged.
T301 supplies characteristic-function terminology, T327 effective enumeration and T335 the fixed-point construction.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
